summary: Duplicate webhook function calls from TS SDK in Cloudflare Worker due to Idempotency-Token truncation by fetch polyfill
description:
Issue summary:
Customer KiteAI reports duplicate outbound webhook invocations for tool/function calls triggered by the Redwood TS SDK when running inside Cloudflare Workers. The duplicates occur after a short reconnect/backoff sequence; scooter shows two identical webhook deliveries with different Idempotency-Token header values (token truncated in one case).

Impact:
- Multiple downstream jobs (payment processing hook) executed twice, causing duplicate invoices for a small subset of requests (~0.4% of calls during peak traffic).
- Customer is on Dedicated plan and requires a mitigation to prevent downstream side effects.

Environment:
- Customer environment: Cloudflare Workers (Edge) using a fetch polyfill (undici/fetch-lite) to call Redwood hosted API via HTTPS through a corporate proxy.
- Redwood side: prod us-east cluster, api-gateway v3, webhook proxy service v1.8.0.
- SDK versions: redwood-sdk@2.4.1 (TS), node-fetch polyfill replaced with fetch-lite @0.3.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1. Deploy a Cloudflare Worker using the TS SDK with streaming responses and function calling enabled.
2. Attach an outbound webhook URL that processes incoming tool calls and triggers idempotent side effects based on the Idempotency-Token header.
3. Simulate intermittent network latency by introducing a proxy-level 200-500ms delay for a subset of requests.
4. Observe webhook deliveries in webhook target logs and Redwood request logs.

Observed behavior:
- For ~0.4% of affected requests, the platform sends two webhook deliveries for the same logical function call.
- Redwood request logs show the first delivery with header "Idempotency-Token: 8a3f...f2d9" and the second delivery with a truncated token header "Idempotency-Token: 8a3f..." (length shorter, missing suffix).
- The truncated token does not match the original idempotency key stored in downstream service, so duplicate processing occurs.

Expected behavior:
- Idempotency-Token should be preserved end-to-end (SDK -> API -> webhook proxy -> customer webhook) and identical across retries/reconnects. Downstream should gracefully deduplicate.

Logs / artifacts attached by customer:
- Excerpt from worker logs: "fetch to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat responded 200, stream closed, reconnecting (attempt 2)"
- Webhook receiver logs with timestamps showing two POSTs 1.2s apart; headers included.
- SDK request trace ID: trace-redwood-990123-1 (customer-provided).

Repro code snippet (customer):
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: SECRET, baseUrl: 'https://api.redwood.ai' });
addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  event.respondWith(handle(event));
});
async function handle(event) {
  const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'gpt-redwood-1-large', messages: [...] , stream: true, functions: [...] , idempotencyKey: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12)).toString() });
  // uses fetch-lite under the hood in the worker
  return new Response('ok');
}

Notes:
- Customer indicates they did not set a custom proxy header and rely on SDK idempotencyKey parameter.
- The issue is only observed from edge worker deployments (not Node.js server deployments).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Patel (Support): Initial triage. Confirmed duplicate webhook deliveries in customer-supplied logs. Requested full request/response headers and trace IDs. Asked customer to provide Worker script and SDK version (received).

2026-03-11 - Ethan Cole (SRE): Pulled request traces for trace-redwood-990123-1. Observed two successful webhook proxy handoffs for same root request. First delivery includes full-length Idempotency-Token, second delivery includes truncated token (length 40 vs 64). Noted both deliveries originated from same Redwood request id with different retry sequence numbers.

2026-03-11 - Dev (Riley Chen): Hypothesis: fetch polyfill or Cloudflare header normalization is splitting/truncating long custom headers on retry path. Could be HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 conversion or proxy reserialization. Adding tests to reproduce locally with fetch-lite + proxy emulator.

2026-03-12 - Customer (KiteAI - ops@kite.ai): Confirmed they are using fetch-lite due to Worker environment limitations. Said duplicates started after SDK upgrade to 2.4.1 and coincided with a recently-added 64-byte idempotency key format. Would accept a short-term workaround.

2026-03-12 - Ethan Cole (SRE): Temporary mitigation suggested to customer: set SDK client option 'idempotencyKeyShortening: true' to emit 32-char keys; or explicitly set a shorter idempotencyKey in the request. Also suggested upgrade to redwood-sdk@2.4.2-beta which contains additional logging. Customer applying workaround now.

2026-03-13 - Riley Chen (Engineer): Reproduced locally: when using fetch-lite behind an http/2 proxy shim, header values >48 chars get truncated on retry path if request is resent using a reconstructed Headers object. Created PR to add header-length normalization and preserve original header raw bytes across retry codepaths. PR referenced below.
2026-03-13 - Maya Patel (Support): Updating ticket with next steps and scheduling follow-up with customer once patch is deployed to staging.
investigation_notes: Edge-only: Not reproducible in Node 18 with node-fetch/undici; reproducible with fetch-lite + http/2 proxy shim.

Header length cutoff observed at ~48 characters in our proxy shim during retry/resend path. Likely caused by Headers serialization path that uses split/join and drops suffix when encountering binary-safe conversion issues.
Retry path reconstructs outbound request headers from an internal map; bug in reconstruction code truncates long header values when composed from multiple Uint8Array chunks.
No indication of intentional behavior from Cloudflare; likely introduced by fetch polyfill + proxy interaction in customer's environment.
Related to SDK retry logic that attempts to replay request on reconnect; idempotency token should be copied verbatim but was being rebuilt incorrectly.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: customer set explicit short idempotencyKey (32 chars) in production which reduced duplicates to 0.0% for observed window. Engineering action: merged fix to SDK retry header reconstruction (PR github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ts/pull/412). Patch will be included in redwood-sdk@2.4.2 release and a hotfix rollout to api-gateway/webhook-proxy to better log header mismatches. Follow-up tasks:
- Deploy SDK 2.4.2 and monitor 24h.
- Add Canary test in CI to run SDK in fetch-lite environment emulation.
- Update edge runbook in Confluence with guidance: "If running in constrained edge runtimes, prefer short idempotency keys (<=40 chars) until SDK 2.4.2 is deployed."
next_steps: 2026-03-13: Release redwood-sdk@2.4.2 with header reconstruction fix (Engineer: Riley Chen).
2026-03-13: Roll out improved logging in webhook-proxy (SRE: Ethan Cole) to detect truncated idempotency tokens and emit alert when mismatch rate >0.1%.
2026-03-14: Customer follow-up call to confirm fix in production (Support: Maya Patel).
